items.mnemonic: A TREE trunk takes STRIKE after STRIKE from the planer until it falls apart into thin, flat boards—each board one SHEET to count.
The tailor sews new CLOTHES for a PERSON who returns at every SUN-rise on tired WALKING LEGS asking for the very same coat, so she stitches a DUPLICATE.
A heavy sack of letters makes the carrier's shoulder DROOP as he trudges into TOWN; the day's MAIL has arrived.
One PERSON stands in the MIDDLE of two quarreling friends, holding a hand of each until they laugh again—patching up the RELATIONSHIP.
SMALL sparks of light spill over the COVER stretched above a young TREE, and in that glow its branches FLOURISH.
A thin strip of TREE wood swings from a FISHHOOK on a string tied to the branch—a TAG with the price scratched on it.
Beneath the CLIFF a RIGHT HAND saws a fallen TREE into flat, even pieces—a BOARD for the new floor.
A SKELETON rattles in the night wind, and every piece that clicks against another is a BONE.
A PERSON balances a SPOON on top of their HEAD; the moment they LEAN to one side, it slides off.
Under the CORPSE-shaped flap of the letterbox a STEM pokes through: a flower someone paid a courier to DELIVER.
A HUSBAND wearing HORNS on his festival hat lifts a SNAKE that winds around his arm like a ROLL of rope.
Beside the FIRE a DOG howls at the MOON while a second FIRE of embers glows under its paws—soon everything will BURN.
A muddy FOOT steps on a fallen pot LID, then EIGHT more prints wander off across the kitchen floor—a TRACE of who passed.
You WRAP a cloth around a coiled SNAKE until only a round bundle shows; to WRAP is to hide the shape inside.
A HORSE waits with a DROP of sweat on its brow while the KING is inside the hall—it is STATIONED at the gate until he returns.
One BOW crusted with ICE, then another BOW crusted with ICE: frozen strings that snap at a touch—both are WEAK.
A SWORD cuts one THREAD into two, and a MOUTH calls out both names as the ends are tied to each stranger—that is how you INTRODUCE them.
A SMALL BIRD perches at the DOOR every dawn and sings for crumbs, until the baker decides to EMPLOY it as the shop's alarm clock.
One HUSBAND meets another HUSBAND under the same SUN and they swap hats on the spot—a fair EXCHANGE.
A bird's BEAK drops the last coin to FINISH the pile, then bows its HEAD at the bank counter—a DEPOSIT made.
A FIRE roars beneath a LOFTY stack of clay pots on the hilltop kiln—time to BAKE.
Through a BAMBOO GATE the morning SUN falls on a single strip with one word written on it—a message kept SIMPLE.
A STAND holds the book open toward the SUN; TEN pages are read before the bell—one CHAPTER each morning.
Under the MOON a RETAINER lies on a BED of GRASS with a HALBERD across his chest, guarding what beats beneath—every INTERNAL ORGAN.
Every STEP the clerk takes is matched by a stroke of his BRUSH, writing the rules down one by one—this is the LAW.
A SHELL purse, HORNS of ribbon, a box as wide as a RICE FIELD, all handed over at SUN-down—a GIFT for the wedding.
The SUN flashes off a raised SWORD, a MOUTH shouts, and a FIRE below throws sparks—together they ILLUMINATE the whole courtyard.
GRASS floats on WATER above a SEEDBED only an INCH deep—the soil here is THIN.
The shepherd waves a BROOM in one STROKE, opens his MOUTH to whistle, and every SHEEP comes running—a FLOCK.
A GRAIN of rice is split into a SMALL sliver with one quick STROKE of the knife—done in a SECOND.
One STROKE of a lantern lights the FRAME of a doorway; past the RICE sacks a BIG room opens—the INTERIOR of the old house.
SAY nothing, the SAMURAI orders, as he stuffs rice into the MOUTH of every sack until it bulges—PACK it tight.
One RIGHT HAND clasps another RIGHT HAND, mirror images gripping tight—a matched PAIR.
A FRAME around a thorny TREE, and a SWORD leaning on it—brush past and the thorns STAB your sleeve.
A white THREAD lies on the soil beside an EARTHWORM, and not a speck of dirt clings to it—it stays PURE.
A bird folds its FEATHERS and takes its STAND on the fence to wait for dawn—THE FOLLOWING day begins.
A HEART sweeps itself clean with a tiny BROOM, then takes a BIG breath of morning air—a PLEASANT feeling.
A SLAB of wood split down the middle: you hold only the left half, flat on one face—ONE-SIDED.

examples.en: one side, one of a pair

items.mnemonic: He kneels on the GRASS, a WRAP of cloth over his shoulders, MOUTH closed, as the drum sounds its STRIKE—a gesture of RESPECT.
A HEART sprouts HORNS of anxiety and sinks into a CONTAINER marked with a CROSS—it cannot stop its WORRY.
White foam rises where the SPRING pushes up through the rock; cup your hands and drink from the SPRING.
WATER churns as a FISH flashes beneath the boat and the net drops—a day of FISHING.
GRASS has swallowed the DECEASED farmer's field and the RIVER has jumped its banks—the land has turned ROUGH.
SHELL money is hidden under the ROOF, hung from a single NAIL where no one thinks to look—the family SAVINGS.
A STONE lies ONE whole day in the SUN until a CROSS-shaped crack spreads across it, yet it will not crumble—it is HARD.
Shovel EARTH over the old well at the edge of the VILLAGE until nothing shows—BURY it.
A TREE trunk with a DROP of candle wax on its crown stands beside the KING's throne—the hall's great PILLAR.
Under a full MOON a RIGHT HAND lays meat on the ALTAR, drums roll and lanterns sway—the FESTIVAL has begun.
A PERSON pushes a STAKE through the knotted neck of a bundle of CLOTHES and slings it over one shoulder—a makeshift BAG.
A length of BAMBOO with a tuft of hair bound on as the BRUSH, dipped in black ink—the classic WRITING BRUSH.
SAY the lesson aloud and let it flow like a RIVER from teacher to pupil—this is INSTRUCTION.
WATER gathers in a warm VALLEY pool and you slip in up to your chin—time to BATHE.
A boy takes his STAND on the rim of the VILLAGE well to see over the crowd—still just a CHILD.
Under the ROOF a single JEWEL glows inside a plain wooden box—the family TREASURE.
EARTH is piled on EARTH and pressed flat with an INCH of wax across the lid—a SEAL no one may break.
By MOON-light a WRAP of bandage covers a CONTAINER-shaped ribcage marked with a CROSS of tape—right over the CHEST.
A STONE ground down to SMALL grains and swept by a single STROKE of wind across the dune—SAND.
The RETAINER holds up his RIGHT HAND and refuses the SHELL money offered as a bribe—a WISE man.
Under the MOON, beneath a low ROOF, you spend the whole EVENING carving a SEAL; by midnight your ARM aches.
The diviner heats a tortoise shell and watches the cracks spread; in their pattern she reads the OMEN.
Inside the LEAN-TO a TREE is split into planks and laid flat underfoot—the first FLOOR.
A THREAD swept up by a BROOM and rinsed in WATER comes out the color of new leaves—GREEN.
HORNS of smoke curl from the SAKE JAR as it is lifted an INCH toward the shrine—an offering to someone REVERED.
Before the ALTAR a MOUTH sings out and LEGS dance in a circle—time to CELEBRATE.
The SPEAR shaft is cut from a young TREE that bends instead of snapping—SOFT wood, supple in the hand.
A CORPSE-still guard, TWENTY steps of stone, EIGHT pillars, and a WEAPON rack at the door—the lord's PALACE.
WATER drips over a CURVE of rock into a SCALLOP shell until the broth inside turns dark and THICK.
A long THREAD is knotted once for every year and coils like a SNAKE across the floor—the family CHRONICLE.
The mover carries a DOOR off its hinges under the MOON, balanced on one SHOULDER.
A BOAR noses under the TREE, splits a fallen peach and crunches straight to the hard stone at its NUCLEUS.
A TREE frame, TWO HANDS on the crank, and a HALBERD blade spinning as the gear—a crude MACHINE.
Cut a TREE into THREE lengths; one PERSON props up the CLOTHESLINE with the longest—a sturdy STICK.
A TREE post at the WEST edge of the village with a small ALTAR nailed to it—a SIGN for travelers.
A DRUM beats beside the sapling and the gardener marks every INCH it grows, until the TREE towers over the village.
WATER fills a sheltered cove beside the CRAFT yard where boats are built—a quiet INLET.
By the WATER a WHITE paper lantern glows at the inn door—a place to STAY OVERNIGHT.
WATER on every side and the boat right in the MIDDLE of it, land gone from view—the OPEN SEA.
WATER splits at a STROKE of rock beneath the CLIFF, and each stream wears CLOTHES of a different color—each branch its own FACTION.
WATER rolls in where an AXE lies forgotten on ONE flat rock and EIGHT gulls pick at the sand—the BEACH.
WATER so low that one HALBERD and a second HALBERD stuck in the riverbed still show their blades—SHALLOW.
WATER streams down the DOOR where a BIG goodbye was said—TEARS.
WATER sealed under a LID; a PERSON tips it at EVENING and a single STROKE of it pours out—LIQUID.
WATER poured from a jar with a LID; one MOUTH sips and a SMALL breeze lifts off the surface—how COOL.
WATER dries under the SUN while the laundry hangs in a ROW, still dripping—everything is DAMP.
WATER seeps from under the CLIFF where a WHITE pebble sits in a SMALL pool—the river's SOURCE.
WATER drips from the ROOF of a hut deep in the VALLEY as the spring snow begins to MELT.
WATER beads on the STAND, slides down the FRAME, counts TEN beats, and lands in an open MOUTH—DRIP.
